description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Koper for car carriers, container ships and bulk carriers: hull structure, ESP gauging and scrubber piping checks.
h1: Ultrasonic Thickness Measurement for Ships in Koper, Slovenia
intro: Koper is Slovenia's only international cargo port and a rail-connected gateway to Austria, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic. Car carriers, container ships, large bulk carriers and tankers call on working schedules, with little lay-by time and no major drydock in the port. Our team travels from India to gauge them alongside or at anchor in the Gulf of Trieste, with the work fitted to the cargo window.
keywords: ultrasonic thickness measurement for ships in koper

highlights.h: A steady flow of car carriers
highlights.p: Koper's car terminal brings a steady flow of car carriers, whose car decks, hoistable decks and ramps take repeated vehicle loads and need deck-by-deck gauging planned around the stevedores' discharge and loading sequence.

highlights.h: Bulk carriers for central European industry
highlights.p: Large bulk carriers discharge iron ore and coal for the hinterland's steel and power plants, and their cargo holds, topside tanks and hatch covers can be gauged once discharge is complete and the holds are cleared.
With no major ship-repair yard in the port, gauging here means using a cargo call well: closing out survey items, building pre-docking estimates or checking condition before a sale or charter.

port.h: The port of Koper and its hinterland trades
p: The port of Koper is operated by Luka Koper, which runs the terminals under a concession covering the whole port. It sits on the Slovenian coast at the south-eastern corner of the Gulf of Trieste, a short drive from the Italian border, and serves a hinterland that reaches far beyond Slovenia: rail lines carry containers, cars and bulk cargo to Austria, Hungary, Slovakia and the Czech Republic. The traffic mix is broad: a container terminal with deep-sea and feeder services, one of the Mediterranean's main car terminals, a dry bulk terminal for iron ore, coal and other cargoes for central European industry, and liquid cargo terminals for petroleum products and chemicals.

That mix brings a wide variety of ships, all of them on working calls. Car carriers load and discharge vehicles over a day or two, container ships exchange boxes and sail, bulk carriers discharge ore or coal for the steel and power plants of the hinterland, and product and chemical tankers discharge at the liquid terminals. Koper has no major ship-repair yard of its own, so dockings happen elsewhere and gauging in Koper is about using the call well: closing out items from the last survey, building pre-docking estimates, or checking a ship's condition for a sale or a charter.

Car carriers bring a type of inspection demand distinctive to a port with a large car terminal. Their multiple car decks, hoistable decks, internal ramps and stern and side ramps carry repeated vehicle loads and suffer from condensation and from salt brought aboard on cars and trucks, while their ballast tanks sit low in a tall, lightly built hull. Gauging on a car carrier during cargo operations has to work around vehicle movements, so it is usually planned deck by deck with the stevedores. Large bulk carriers at the bulk terminal raise the ESP side of the work, with cargo hold and ballast tank gauging tied to their renewal surveys.

facilities.h: Where thickness gauging happens at the port of Koper
p: All Koper gauging is done afloat, at the terminals or at anchor. At the car terminal, deck and ramp gauging on car carriers is sequenced with the vehicle discharge and loading plan; at the container terminal, ballast tanks, hatch covers and scrubber piping are gauged around crane work; at the bulk terminal, holds become accessible once discharge is complete and the stevedores have cleared them. Each terminal has its own access and safety rules, and the ship's agent coordinates permits, passes and timing with Luka Koper so that the team is on board when the spaces open up.

Ships waiting for a berth anchor in the Gulf of Trieste, where launch access makes pre-purchase, on-hire and off-hire gauging possible without occupying a berth. When gauging in Koper is a prelude to a docking, the nearest ship-repair yards are a short distance away, including Viktor Lenac near Rijeka in Croatia, and the technicians can move on with the ship to the yard. Trieste and Monfalcone, across the gulf in Italy, can be covered in the same mobilisation when a fleet has ships in more than one north Adriatic port.

Container terminal, Luka Koper — hatch coaming, cross-deck and ballast tank gauging plus scrubber outlet checks on deep-sea container ships
Dry bulk terminal — large bulk carriers emptied of iron ore or coal, with holds, hopper and topside tanks and hatch covers then open for readings
Liquid cargo terminals — deck, deck piping and accessible ballast tank gauging on product and chemical tankers within the cargo window
Gulf of Trieste anchorage — ships awaiting a Koper berth, boarded by launch for buyers' inspections and on-hire or off-hire gauging

context.h: Port state control, emissions and the Koper hinterland trades
p: Slovenia carries out port state control in Koper as a member of the Paris MoU. The Gulf of Trieste lies within the Mediterranean SOx ECA, which took effect on 1 May 2025, so ships berthing at Koper use 0.10% sulphur fuel or a scrubber achieving an equivalent result. Many deep-sea container ships and car carriers calling at Koper make long passages from Asia, and for scrubber-fitted ships the system now stays on from the moment they pass into the Mediterranean; their wash-water and overboard piping is worth gauging on regular calls rather than leaving until the next docking.

Koper calls fall under EU ETS, which brought shipping in from 2024, and FuelEU Maritime, which started in 2025, as at any EU port, and they add weight to fleet-renewal decisions in the car carrier and bulk sectors, where older ships compete with newer, more efficient tonnage. A sale, recycling or life-extension decision on an older car carrier or bulk carrier rests on knowing the steel condition. Slovenia shares Schengen membership and the euro with Italy and Croatia, and Koper's position next to both borders makes it a natural part of a north Adriatic mobilisation covering several ports.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Koper
jobs.p: Koper jobs fit inside cargo calls. A car carrier's discharge and loading, a container exchange or a bulk discharge gives a defined window, and the scope is agreed in advance so the team can work through it in the order the terminal allows. Where a ship calls regularly, larger programmes are split across calls; where a docking follows, the readings go straight into the yard specification.
list: Car carrier thickness gauging of hoistable decks, internal ramps and the stern ramp at the Koper car terminal, planned deck by deck with the stevedores
Bulk carrier ESP gauging of cargo holds and topside tanks after iron ore discharge, as pre-docking input ahead of the ship's third renewal survey
Container ship at the Koper container terminal: scrubber wash-water line and outlet readings, repeated on the next rotation to show the rate of loss
Product tanker at the liquid cargo terminal: deck plating and the ballast tanks the crew can open, gauged to follow up substantial corrosion recorded at the last survey
Pre-purchase condition gauging on a car carrier at anchor in the Gulf of Trieste, covering whichever spaces the crew can open safely while it waits

logistics: Ljubljana Jože Pučnik Airport is Slovenia's main airport, and Trieste Airport and Venice Marco Polo are also within road distance, which gives a choice of flights for arrivals from India. Access to the terminals runs through Luka Koper's port security procedures, with passes requested by the ship's agent, who also books launches for ships at anchor. Entry to Slovenia, a Schengen state, is on Schengen visas for our India-based technicians. Car carrier and container calls usually follow known rotations, which helps with planning, and we confirm the berth window with the agent before the team travels.

faqs.q: Can you gauge car decks on a car carrier during cargo operations in Koper?
faqs.a: Yes, in coordination with the stevedores. Decks being worked are off limits, so we gauge decks that are empty or not yet in use and move as the discharge or loading progresses. Hoistable decks, ramps and their supporting structure are planned with the chief officer in advance so that the readings fit around vehicle movements.

faqs.q: Is there a drydock in Koper?
faqs.a: No major ship-repair yard operates in the port, so gauging in Koper is done afloat. If the readings are feeding a docking, Viktor Lenac in Rijeka and other north Adriatic yards are a road journey away, and the technicians who measured the ship in Koper can continue at the yard so both sets of readings match.

faqs.q: Can ship inspection in Koper be combined with Trieste or Rijeka?
faqs.a: Yes. Trieste is a short drive across the Italian border and Rijeka is reachable by road in Croatia, and a single Schengen visa covers all three countries. When a fleet has ships at more than one north Adriatic port in the same period, we sequence the work into one mobilisation and report each ship separately.

faqs.q: What gauging is useful on a bulk carrier discharging iron ore in Koper?
faqs.a: Once the holds are discharged and cleared, cargo hold frames, hopper and topside tank plating, and hatch covers and coamings can be gauged, along with ballast tanks the ship makes safe. Ore cargoes are heavy and abrasive, so hold structure and tank tops deserve attention, particularly ahead of a renewal survey under the ESP rules.
